dedupe_keys.name: aurora airport resiliency plan for a cascadia earthquake oregon

description: The Aurora Airport Resiliency Plan was prepared by the Aurora Airport Improvement Association (June 2021, updated 30 August 2024) and submitted as public testimony to the Oregon Legislature in 2025. It describes the role the airport and its surroundings could play after a major disaster, above all a magnitude 8 to 9 Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake, when roads and rail lines are cut by landslides, broken pavement and unusable bridges and air transport must carry supplies, medical help and crews to repair bridges, power lines and gas lines. It gives the airport's history and assets: a runway lengthened from 4,104 to 5,004 feet in 1995 on a heavy rock base built for military use, a control tower operating since 2015, and about 325 acres split between the State of Oregon (45%) and private owners (55%), plus geotechnical cone penetration tests and runway load capacity checked with the FAA method. Coverage: one general aviation airport south of Portland serving north Marion and nearby counties. Access: a PDF on the legislature's site. Licence and cost: public document, free. Caveats: an advocacy document by an airport users' association supporting a runway extension, not an independent assessment. It illustrates emergency response and recovery planning around airports as disaster logistics hubs. It relates to the airport disaster relief cargo model and the FAA NPIAS in the catalogue.
